name: The Hungering Dark
summary: Chapter 5 of The Seven Teeth of Vashkul, the finale. The Cantor has retreated to the Maw with every Tooth the Choir holds and begun the Choir of Teeth. The hero must break the siege of Lantern Hold, cross the haunted Blightwood, perhaps ring the Drowned Abbey’s bells, descend the Maw and face Seraphine Vell at the Jaw-Stone, where every Tooth carried is both a key to the seal and a prize she can steal. How the Maw ends depends on everything that came before.

chapters.name: The Hungering Dark
chapters.summary: Lantern Hold, the Blightwood, the drowned bells and the Maw: the Choir of Teeth and the final seal.

scenes.name: The Siege of Lantern Hold
scenes.seed: Lantern Hold, the Wardens’ fortress on its island of black stone, is ringed by the plague-dead. They stand waist-deep in the fen in their thousands, swaying to a song only they can hear, and every night they come a little closer to the walls. To the south the sky over the Maw is black at noon.

variants.seed: Briarkin archers and cured Hollowmere folk man the walls beside Grell’s Wardens, green ribbons on their bows. Nobody here has forgotten who brought the cure.
Grell’s Wardens stand alone, grey with exhaustion. The Briarkin sent no one: the fen remembers the pyres of Hollowmere.
Among the dead in the water you recognise faces from Hollowmere: the people nobody saved, singing now for the Choir.
The Wardens hold the walls alone, and do not know whether Hollowmere still lives.
Behind the dead, on a raft of lashed coffins, Mother Sallow is preaching. “Come home,” she sings, and the dead sway toward the Hold.
A rider from the war council reached the Hold last night: the Dawn Lance is coming, three hours behind you.
The Wardens greet you as the one who trusted them with the Tooth of Want. Even Grell nods.
The Hold’s courtyard is full of cure-tents that smell of bitterroot and bell-ash.
Pyres burn in the Hold’s courtyard day and night. The Wardens still fight the Sickness the only way they know.
A basket of thorn-charms waits for you at the gate, sent by Grandmother Wick “for the ones going down the hole.”
Lantern Hold has fallen. Its lanterns are out, and the survivors huddle on the causeway.

actions.label: Carry lantern-oil to the walls

success.text: You and the Wardens run the heavy oil-casks up the stair and fill the ditches below the wall. When the dead come, the fen itself will burn.

failure.text: A cask slips on the wet stair and bursts. There is not enough oil left for the ditches.

actions.label: Rally the exhausted Wardens

advantageIf.source: The Wardens trust the one who gave them the Tooth of Want

success.text: You stand on a cask in the courtyard and tell them what is at the bottom of the Maw. When you finish, Grell draws her sword, and every Warden in the Hold lifts a lantern.

failure.text: They listen, but they are too tired to hope. Grell thanks you, curtly, and goes back to the wall.

actions.label: Hold the walls against the dead

outcome.text: At dusk the song rises, and the dead come up out of the fen all at once.

actions.label: Drag Mother Sallow out of the water alive

outcome.text: Sallow lets herself be dragged out of the fen, still smiling. “She wears the Queen’s-godmother ring, you know,” she says. “She will sing you to sleep.” The Wardens chain her in the Hold’s cellar.

actions.label: Finish Mother Sallow

outcome.text: Mother Sallow sinks into the black water, still singing, and the song stops.

actions.label: Rest in the Hold before the march south

outcome.text: The Wardens give you the captain’s own cot. You sleep with the Hold’s lanterns burning all night on the walls.

exits.label: Take the causeway to the Drowned Abbey

scenes.name: The Blightwood Crossing
scenes.seed: The Blightwood: grey trees weeping black sap, moss that whispers when you step on it, and paths that are never where they were an hour ago. Something with too many eyes keeps pace with you just out of sight. Beyond the wood lies the Maw.

variants.seed: After dark the paths move. You can hear them doing it: a slow creak of roots, like a ship at anchor.
Nettle has gone quiet. This was her grandmother’s wood before the Maw woke; she touches the grey trees as she passes, like graves.
Briarkin curse-marks are cut into the trees: the clans have not forgiven the burning of Wick. Someone is hunting you in here.
A thorn-token from Grandmother Wick hangs at your belt. Where it points, the brambles part.
Sometimes you catch the smell of salt and rotten kelp in the wood, which is wrong. The sea hag’s family has not forgotten your bargain.
Wick’s voice in your ear, from nowhere: “You owe me, dearie. Spare the old green thing at the heart of the wood.”
The heart-tree stands open in its clearing, vast and grey, its roots in black water.

actions.label: Follow your guide through the moving paths

outcome.text: Nettle — or Wick’s thorn-token — knows the old ways. The paths stop shifting under your feet.

actions.label: Find a way through the wood by daylight

success.text: You mark the trees with chalk and keep the sun on your left. By afternoon you find the old Briarkin path to the heart.

failure.text: You walk for hours and come back to your own chalk marks.

actions.label: Find a way through the wood in the dark

success.text: You follow the creak of the moving roots against the wind, and it leads you to the old Briarkin path.

failure.text: The paths move behind you. By the time you stop, you are deeper in than when you started.

actions.label: Walk through the whispering grove

advantageIf.source: Thaloren’s blessing from the Millbrook shrine

success.text: The moss whispers your name in a cultured, sad voice. You keep walking, and it gives up.

failure.text: The whispers get in. For an hour you hear only her: “You will never want again.” When it stops, you are shaking, and part of you is still listening.

actions.label: Fight through to the heart-tree

outcome.text: The shambling mound rises out of the black water at the heart-tree’s foot, and the many-eyed wolves close in.

actions.label: Fight through to the heart-tree

outcome.text: The shambling mound rises at the heart-tree’s foot, the wolves close in — and Briarkin arrows come out of the trees. The curse-hunters have found you.

actions.label: Keep Wick’s bargain: spare the mound, fight the wolves

outcome.text: You lower your weapon to the old green thing at the heart-tree. It sinks back into the water. The wolves do not.

actions.label: Keep Wick’s bargain: spare the mound, fight the wolves

outcome.text: You spare the old green thing at the heart-tree, and it sinks back into the water. The wolves and the curse-hunters do not.

actions.label: Help Nettle heal the heart-tree

success.text: You cut the black rot from the heart-tree’s roots while Nettle sings to it. Near the end she stops, and says a word you have never heard, and the tree answers. “That’s my name,” she whispers. “Gran kept it in a jar. The tree kept it better.”

failure.text: The rot goes deeper than your knife. The heart-tree does not answer yet.

actions.label: Trade the Tooth of Want for your stolen memory

outcome.text: The hag’s sister takes the Tooth of Want in her grey fingers and presses her lips to your forehead. The memory the sea hag took comes back all at once, and you weep. Then she is gone, and so is the Tooth: she will sell it to the Choir before dawn.

actions.label: Refuse the hag and fight

outcome.text: “Pity,” says the hag’s sister, and the dark between the trees opens around her.

exits.label: Turn aside to the Drowned Abbey

scenes.name: The Drowned Bells
scenes.seed: The Drowned Abbey of Mireth, half-sunk in the fen. Its nine dead-bells hang in the flooded undercroft, green with age. The old books say that if all nine ring together at midnight, the Maw’s song falters.

variants.seed: Abbot Cendric meets you at the door with a lantern. “I have waited my whole life to ring them,” he says.
Nobody keeps the Abbey now. The Abbot’s lantern hangs cold by the door.
The Drowned Tooth hums in your pack, and far below, the bells hum back.
It is midnight. The water in the undercroft is perfectly still.
The bells have rung. Somewhere to the south, the Maw’s song stumbles.

actions.label: Keep vigil until midnight

outcome.text: You wait out the day and the evening in the cold nave, listening to the water.

actions.label: Let Abbot Cendric lead the rite

outcome.text: Cendric speaks the old rite of Mireth in a voice that does not shake. The water in the undercroft begins to glow.

actions.label: Speak the rite of Mireth yourself

advantageIf.source: The Drowned Tooth makes the bells resonate

success.text: You find the words in the Abbot’s mouldering breviary and speak them into the water. The undercroft begins to glow.

failure.text: You stumble over the old words, and the water stays dark. You try again.

actions.label: Dive to free a sunken bell

advantageIf.source: The Drowned Tooth makes the bells resonate

success.text: You go down into the black water and drag a sunken bell upright on its chain.

failure.text: The cold closes your throat. You come up gasping, without the bell.

actions.label: Ring all nine bells

outcome.text: The nine bells ring together, and every drowned dead thing in the Abbey wakes to stop them.

actions.label: Rest in the dry cells of the upper Abbey

outcome.text: You sleep in a monk’s cell above the flood, under Mireth’s cracked window.

exits.label: Take the fen road to the Blightwood
Take the known path through the wood to the Maw

scenes.name: The Maw
scenes.seed: The Maw: a sinkhole a mile across, breathing. Warm air comes up out of it in long slow exhalations that smell of bile and old iron, and the Choir’s song rises with it. A spiral stair cut by imperial delvers fourteen centuries ago winds down into the dark.

variants.seed: Pyrraxis lies coiled on the far rim, gorged and dozing on the Tooth you paid her. She does not care who wins.
Far above, Pyrraxis circles the Maw, screaming, and the Choir’s song rises to meet her.
The Wardens’ old map is in your hand: every turn of the stair, every bile-pool, every sentry post.
Behind you, Grell’s Wardens are lighting lanterns around the whole rim. “We hold the top,” she says. “You hold the rest.”
At the bottom of the stair, a thin figure with sewn eyes waits at the sanctum gate: Vosk the Hollow, making his final stand.
Nettle is gone. You saw her running down the stair ahead of you, toward the song.

actions.label: Follow the Wardens’ map down

outcome.text: The map takes you down the spiral stair and around the bile-pools by a delvers’ ledge nobody else remembers.

actions.label: Find a way down through the dark

success.text: You follow the warm draught down the spiral stair and find a delvers’ ledge that skirts the bile-pools.

failure.text: The stair splits and splits again. You come down into a cavern of black bile pools — and something in the pools moves.

actions.label: Fight your way across the bile-pools

outcome.text: The chuuls rise out of the bile, clicking.

actions.label: Slip past the Choir’s sentries

success.text: The sentries in the gallery are singing with their eyes closed. You pass close enough to smell the bile on their robes.

failure.text: A bone chime rings in the gallery. The singing stops, and every sentry turns toward you.

actions.label: Attack the sentry gallery

outcome.text: The Choir’s fanatics come at you along the gallery with the dead behind them.

actions.label: Attack the sentry gallery

outcome.text: The Choir’s fanatics come at you along the gallery, and behind them Vosk the Hollow raises his hands.

actions.label: Face Vosk at the sanctum gate

outcome.text: “You again,” says Vosk at the sanctum gate. “Of course. Let us finish it.”

actions.label: Take Vosk alive

outcome.text: Vosk sits down on the sanctum steps. “I only wanted to understand it,” he says. You bind his hands; the Wardens can collect him from the rim.

actions.label: Finish Vosk

outcome.text: Vosk the Hollow falls down the last of the stair into the dark, and the Choir loses its archivist.

actions.label: Go through the sanctum gate

outcome.text: Past the sanctum gate the Choir kept its stores. You find two flasks of Warden-brewed healing among the offerings, and below, you hear her voice at last.

scenes.name: The Choir of Teeth
scenes.seed: At the bottom of the Maw is a jaw. The Jaw-Stone rises out of the black bile like the lower jaw of something the size of a cathedral, with seven sockets along its rim, and in front of it a woman in the grey robes of an almoner conducts a choir of the dead. Every Tooth the Choir holds is already in its socket, glowing. The Maw breathes in time with her song.

variants.seed: You know her face: Lady Seraphine Vell, Royal Almoner of Aurelmark, the Queen’s godmother. She says your name as if she is glad to see you.
You have never seen her face before. She knows yours. “You came all this way,” she says kindly, “and you still do not know who I am.”
You know her voice, though: it is the voice from the barrow at Millbrook, the one that promised you would never want again.
When she sees Aurek her song breaks for a heartbeat. “Oh, my dear,” she says. “Not you.”
Aurek Vell stands at his aunt’s side, pale, his staff lit. He will not meet your eyes.
A tiefling in a Choir robe edges along the Jaw-Stone toward you, not quite smiling: Rook Marrowby, sent to steal the rest of your Teeth. He looks ashamed.
Five sockets or more are full, and something cold and hungry is climbing up out of the Jaw to meet you.
All seven sockets are full. The Jaw is opening. If the song ends like this, the Maw opens with it.
Far above, faint, the drowned bells are still ringing, and every time they ring the Choir misses a beat.
Seraphine is at bay against the Jaw-Stone, bleeding, one verse left in her.
The Jaw-Stone is empty. Her voice comes up out of the Maw’s throat now, from everywhere.

actions.label: Talk Rook back to your side

success.text: “Partner,” Rook says, and then, “Boss.” He laughs, a little wildly, and turns around, and starts working at the Jaw-Stone with a crowbar.

failure.text: “Sorry, partner,” Rook says, and his hand is in your pack before you see it move. Then he is gone into the dark toward the Jaw-Stone.

actions.label: Hold on to the Teeth with all your strength

advantageIf.source: The drowned bells still ring in the Maw

disadvantageIf.source: The Choir’s song is nearly finished

success.text: The Maw pulls at the Teeth you carry like a tide. You hold on, and the pull breaks.

failure.text: The Maw pulls, and something in your pack tears loose.

Nettle taught you what her whisper sounds like

success.text: You get your fingers under the Tooth of Want and heave. It comes out of the socket with a sound like a pulled tooth, and the whole Maw screams.

failure.text: The Tooth of Want will not move, and the Jaw-Stone bites back.

actions.label: Let Aurek speak to his aunt

outcome.text: Aurek walks past you to the Jaw-Stone and takes his aunt’s bloody hand. He does not argue; he tells her about Liesel, the little sister she never talks about, and about the Queen, who still loves her. Seraphine looks at him for a long time. Then she turns to the Jaw-Stone, and begins to sing the other way: the reverse-song, her own voice turning the ritual inward to shut the jaw she opened.

actions.label: Show her Liesel’s locket

advantageIf.source: Aurek told you Liesel’s whole story
You know what the Dawn Lance did at Cinderdale

success.text: You open the locket and hold it up so she can see the painted face inside: a little girl, eight years old, who starved in the Ashfall Winter. “She would not have wanted this,” you say. “Not for anyone.” Seraphine takes the locket, and her song stops. Then she turns to the Jaw-Stone, and begins to sing the other way: the reverse-song, her own voice turning the ritual inward to shut the jaw she opened.

failure.text: She looks at the locket, and something in her face closes. “Liesel is the reason,” she says. “Liesel is the whole reason.” She will not listen again.

actions.label: Give her Queen Isolde’s letter

outcome.text: Seraphine reads Isolde’s letter twice. “She remembers the lullabies,” she says, and her voice cracks. “I sang them to her when she was sick.” Then she turns to the Jaw-Stone, and begins to sing the other way: the reverse-song, her own voice turning the ritual inward to shut the jaw she opened.

actions.label: Offer her no mercy

outcome.text: You say nothing. She understands.

actions.label: Strike her down

outcome.text: Seraphine Vell dies at the foot of the Jaw-Stone with the last verse unsung. Around you the dead stop singing, one by one, and lie down in the bile.

actions.label: Strike to subdue her, and take her alive

outcome.text: You knock Seraphine Vell senseless with the flat of your weapon, and the last verse dies in her throat. She will stand trial in Highcrown, before the Queen she loves.

exits.label: Set the Teeth back into the jaw

scenes.name: The Final Seal
scenes.seed: The Jaw-Stone waits. The Teeth that you and your allies carried here are laid out on its rim; the ones the Choir set are still glowing in their sockets. To seal the Maw you must put the Teeth back the way the founders did: in reverse, root upward, and sing them home.

variants.seed: Seraphine stands at the Jaw-Stone beside you, mute with effort, singing the other way.
Seraphine lies bound on the stone behind you, awake, listening.
Seraphine’s body lies at the foot of the Jaw-Stone.
Her voice rises out of the Maw’s throat as you work, trying to sing over you.
All seven sockets are full and glowing. The jaw is already opening.
The Jaw-Stone is shuddering under the reversed Teeth. It will hold.
It is not enough. The jaw closes, but not all the way.

actions.label: Hold the breach as the Maw opens

outcome.text: The seventh socket blazes, and the jaw opens. Vashkul, the Hungering Dark, breathes in, and the whole Gloamfen goes silent.

actions.label: Sing the last Tooth home and close the jaw

outcome.text: The last Tooth goes home. The jaw closes with a sound you feel in your teeth, and the Maw stops breathing. For the first time in fourteen centuries, the Hungering Dark is truly asleep.

actions.label: Close the jaw as far as it will go

outcome.text: You sing until your voice gives out. The jaw closes, almost. A crack of dark remains, and something on the other side of it is still humming.

actions.label: Flee north with the survivors
Hold Seraphine’s hand as the Maw closes
Climb out into a kingdom without a Queen
Climb out into the dawn
Climb out, and listen

npcs.name: Warden-Captain Maud Grell
npcs.personality: Iron-grey, hard as the Hold’s walls, exhausted beyond pride. She burned villages to stop the Sickness and will not apologise, but she will fight beside anyone who fights the dead.
secrets: She has already written her own death notice and left it on her desk.
npcs.voice: Low and rasping, every sentence an order.

npcs.name: Warden-Sergeant Odo Brask
npcs.personality: Dour, decent and loyal to Grell even when he doubts her. Keeps the Wardens’ Teeth in lead boxes.
secrets: He has kept a list of every name burned in the Purge.

npcs.name: Mother Sallow
npcs.personality: Kindly-seeming, grandmotherly, utterly devoted to the Cantor. She thinks of the dead as her children.
secrets: She knows the Cantor wears the Queen’s-godmother ring.

npcs.name: Grandmother Wick
npcs.personality: Ancient, sly, kind in a way that costs. She has come to the Hold to see the end of the Maw with her own eyes.
secrets: She knows the Maw’s true name, and will sing it once.
npcs.voice: Creaking and amused; calls everyone dearie.

npcs.name: Abbot Cendric
npcs.personality: An old priest of Mireth, the last keeper of the Drowned Abbey, who has waited his whole life to ring the dead-bells.
secrets: He is afraid of the water.

npcs.name: The Hag’s Sister
npcs.personality: The sea hag’s elder sister, a night hag who keeps her family’s bargains. Polite, patient, and hungry for Teeth.
secrets: She will sell any Tooth she gets to the Choir before dawn.
npcs.voice: Wet and pleasant, like a kettle about to boil.

npcs.name: Vosk the Hollow
npcs.personality: A renegade Veyran scholar and the Choir’s archivist-mage, eyes sewn shut, courteous and utterly without pity. This is his final stand.
secrets: He no longer believes the Cantor, but has nowhere else to go.
npcs.voice: Dry and scholarly; hums the Choir’s tune between sentences.

npcs.name: Lady Seraphine Vell, the Cantor
npcs.personality: The Royal Almoner of Aurelmark and the Cantor of the Hollow Choir. Warm, tireless, sincere. She starved in the Ashfall Winter and truly believes Vashkul will devour hunger itself. A zealot, not a sadist.
secrets: Her sister Liesel died in her arms in Cinderdale.
The one thing she loves is Queen Isolde.
npcs.voice: Cultured, sad and musical; the voice from the Millbrook dream.

npcs.name: Aurek Vell
npcs.personality: Brilliant, anxious and bookish, and standing beside his aunt because he could not bear not to.
secrets: He would switch sides again if she fell.

npcs.name: Rook Marrowby
npcs.personality: A charming liar who sold you out for his debt, and has regretted it every day since.
secrets: He kept the Choir’s payment and has never spent a coin of it.
npcs.voice: Theatrical and quick, but quieter now.

lose.text: The gate goes down. Mireth’s priests find you under the dead at dawn and breathe you back to life in the Hold’s ruined chapel. Lantern Hold has fallen.

lose.text: You wake at the edge of the Blightwood eight hours later, bitten and bone-tired. The wood has let you go, this once.

encounters.name: The sea hag’s sister
terrain: a circle of bone charms (the hag’s ground)

win.text: The hag’s sister shrieks and folds into the dark between two trees. She will not come back tonight.

lose.text: You wake at dawn in the dead grass with the taste of her nightmares in your mouth. She has had her fun, and gone.

encounters.name: The drowned dead of the bell-well

win.text: The wraith comes apart in the bell-song. The last note rolls out over the fen toward the Maw, and you feel it falter. Mireth’s blessing settles on you like cold water: in the Maw, the dark will find it harder to hold you.

lose.text: The bells go silent. Mireth’s priests drag you up out of the water and breathe life back into you in the upper Abbey. The chance is gone: the bells will not ring again this year.

encounters.name: The bile-pools

win.text: The second chuul sinks back into the bile and does not come up again.

lose.text: The Maw heaves. You are vomited up its throat in a flood of black bile and wake on the rim, retching, an hour later. Something was torn from your pack on the way up.

outcome.text: The exhausted Wardens at the gate give ground, and the gate-bar splinters inward. You are in the crush when it goes.

outcome.text: Warden-Sergeant Brask unwraps the Tooth of Want from its lead box and puts it in your hands. “The Wardens kept it. You carry it the last mile.”

outcome.text: At midnight a grey woman in a sodden shawl steps out from between two trees. She smells of salt and kelp. “My sister kept something of yours,” she says, if you bargained with the sea hag; if you did not, she only smiles, and her teeth are very long.

beats.text: The Maw breathes out.

outcome.text: The Maw breathes out, a long warm gust of bile and rot. Everyone who breathes it in retches and burns.

beats.text: Nettle betrays the party at the rim of the Maw.

outcome.text: At the top of the stair Nettle takes your pack from your shoulder, gently, as if to carry it. “She says it will cure everyone,” she says. “Every sickness, forever.” Then she runs down into the dark with a Tooth in her fist.

beats.text: Nettle confesses the Cantor’s whisper.

outcome.text: “She’s been whispering to me,” Nettle says at the top of the stair. “Since the Blightwood. Says the Maw will cure everyone.” She spits into the dark. “I told her where to put it. Now I know what her voice sounds like, and so do you.”

beats.text: You have reached the bottom of the world.
The Maw spits the party out.
The Cantor sinks into the Maw.

outcome.text: When you reach the Jaw-Stone again it is empty. Seraphine Vell has gone down into the Maw’s throat, still singing, and her voice comes up out of the dark from everywhere at once. The Wardens will have to seal what they can without you.

beats.text: The drowned bells strengthen the seal.

outcome.text: The drowned bells are still ringing far above. The seal takes their note.

beats.text: Dawnbreaker pins the jaw.

outcome.text: Dawnbreaker is driven into the Jaw-Stone’s hinge, and the holy lance pins the jaw.

beats.text: Wick’s Name-Chant binds the seal.

outcome.text: From somewhere in the fen, Grandmother Wick sings the Maw’s true name, and the jaw flinches.

beats.text: Nettle sings the Name-Chant.

outcome.text: Nettle sings the Name-Chant her grandmother would have sung, in her own true name, and the jaw flinches.

beats.text: Aurek’s father’s reverse-song.

outcome.text: You sing the reverse-song from Aurek’s father’s notes, and the Teeth settle deeper.

beats.text: The Wardens hold the rim.

outcome.text: High above, Grell’s Wardens light every lantern on the rim at once. The Maw cannot breathe out.

beats.text: Seraphine’s own voice seals the jaw.

outcome.text: Seraphine sings the reverse-song with her own voice, and it is the strongest voice in the Maw.

beats.text: The Cantor escapes into the Maw.

outcome.text: Through the last crack in the jaw, Seraphine Vell slips down into the dark, singing. She will be the Maw’s voice now.

beats.text: The Whispering Sickness dies with the Maw.

outcome.text: All across the Gloamfen, the sick stop humming. The spores are dying with the Maw.

beats.text: Seraphine survives the sealing, mute.

outcome.text: When the jaw closes, Seraphine is still standing. She opens her mouth, and no sound comes out: the Maw took her voice as its price, and left her the rest.

beats.text: Seraphine dies sealing the Maw.

outcome.text: When the jaw closes, Seraphine sits down against the Jaw-Stone, smiling, and does not get up.

beats.text: The hero holds the breach.

outcome.text: You hold the breach with everyone who still trusts you, long enough for the fen towns to flee north. The Maw kisses you as you go: black veins climb your neck.

scar.description: the Maw’s kiss: black veins on the neck

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Queen Isolde reforms the Almonry, and for the first time in a generation the fen towns are fed.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Dawn Lance holds the regency until a new heir is crowned.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Ironvault’s creditors sit on the regency council, and every decision has a price.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Chamberlain Hale rules as regent, weakly; the great houses are already sharpening knives.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The regency council offers you a seat at its table.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Dawnbreaker hangs in Dawnspire again, and recruits flood the Order of the Dawn Lance.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Among the new knights of the Lance is a miller’s son from Millbrook: Ser Pip Hallard.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Dawn Lance offers you a commission, and asks, politely, for its lance back.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Without Dawnbreaker the Order of the Dawn Lance dwindles to a handful of old knights.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Ser Corwin Ashvale leads the Order now; Aldric Thane keeps its archives.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: With the money trail proven, the Crown’s debts are renegotiated and the deep mines reopen.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Ironvault Consortium calls in its debts, and Aurelmark tightens its belt.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Lantern Wardens lay down their torches and become the healers’ escorts.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Grell is feted in Highcrown for the Purge, but the fens remember the pyres.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: With Lantern Hold fallen, the Wardens scatter across the fen.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: By royal charter the Briarkin are granted the last wild marshes of the Gloamfen.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Nettle leads the grieving Briarkin clans in Wick’s place.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Briarkin vanish into the deep fen and do not come out.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Without the Cantor, the Hollow Choir’s cells collapse one by one.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Hollow Choir goes quiet, and waits for its Cantor to sing again.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Some of the Cantor’s lieutenants are still at large, and still singing.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Seraphine Vell stands trial in Highcrown. You may yet testify for mercy.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Isolde insists on a quiet state funeral for her godmother.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Saltwind charter is reformed after Pell’s exposure, and tariffs are halved.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Governor Pell thrives: corrupt, but stable.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: With Gullhaven occupied, the Saltwind monopoly on the isles is total.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Captain Quint receives a royal pardon, and the Red Gull Brotherhood sails as privateers.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The Brass Parrot’s treasure buys a legendary week-long party at Fennick’s Rest.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Free Gullhaven builds its first warship in a century.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Oswin Tull rebuilds burned Gullhaven, bitterly.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Nettle goes home to the Blightwood with her true name, and the grey trees start to green.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Nettle is never seen again, though fen folk say a halfling sings at the Maw’s rim on moonless nights.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Rook Marrowby buys a sloop and names it after you, then loses it at cards within the year.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Rook Marrowby lies low in the isles, ashamed, and sends you a letter every winter.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Aurek Vell founds a school of Maw-lore in Highcrown, so nobody ever has to learn it the way he did.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Aurek Vell is tried beside his aunt, and does not defend himself.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Millbrook puts up a statue of you on the green, badly carved and much loved.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: Reeve Hollis Tamsin is knighted for raising the Millbrook militia.

beats.text: Epilogue.

outcome.text: The bards call you “the Unkillable”, and argue about how many times you actually died.

deadlines.text: Reach the Jaw-Stone before the Choir of Teeth is sung through
deadlines.warning: The sky over the Maw has gone from black to a deep wet red. The Choir is on its last verses.

missed.text: The song changes key. Everyone in the Gloamfen hears it: the Choir of Teeth is on its final verse. The Maw will pull harder now.

Descend the Maw to the Jaw-Stone
Stop the Cantor’s Choir of Teeth

endings.name: The Hungering Dawn
endings.text: The Maw opens and Vashkul wakes. You and those who trusted you hold the breach long enough for the fen towns to flee north; Aurelmark endures under siege while the Gloamfen falls silent. The long hunger has begun.

endings.name: The Pale Mother’s Mercy
endings.text: Seraphine Vell sings the jaw shut with her own voice while a friend holds her hand. The Maw is sealed and the Whispering Sickness ends. In Highcrown, Queen Isolde weeps for her godmother.

endings.name: The Hollow Throne
endings.text: The Maw is sealed, but the Queen is dead, and a regency council rules an exhausted kingdom. Orrimar is saved; Aurelmark will spend a generation deciding who it belongs to.

endings.name: Dawn over Orrimar
endings.text: The Maw is sealed, the Cantor is defeated and the Queen lives. Bells ring in Highcrown, and Queen Isolde honours you before the whole court.

endings.name: A Quiet Hunger
endings.text: The seal holds, barely. The Sickness wanes but does not end, and some nights the dreams still carry a voice up out of the dark. The Maw is stirring — and something down there is waiting.
